title: How AI is redefining Wall Street jobs — and boosting demand for this new 'hottest skill' by 1,721%
key_facts: PYMNTS reports, citing a CNBC report of Friday 2 Oct 2026 that uses Draup data, that AI-related job postings at banks including JPMorgan Chase, Citigroup and Capital One rose 49% this year to 139,819.

Mentions of 'agent orchestration' (getting several AI agents to work together on one task) in bank job postings rose 1,721%, from 108 in 2025 to 1,967 this year, which the article says is growth from a small base.
Postings mentioning responsible AI rose 657%, AI governance 394% and risk management 359%.

Draup, an enterprise hiring analytics firm, builds its counts from public job listings and platforms such as LinkedIn; its chief executive Vijay Swaminathan called agent orchestration 'arguably the hottest skill on Wall Street'.
Postings citing the LangGraph tool rose 679% and LlamaIndex 291%.
Revised U.S. bank model-risk guidance issued 17 April left generative and agentic AI outside its scope, leaving banks to rely on their own risk practices.
JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon said in May the bank expects to hire more AI specialists and fewer bankers in certain categories.
quote_evidence: References to agent orchestration rose 1,721% in bank job postings this year, the report said.
It grew from a small base, with mentions climbing from 108 in 2025 to 1,967 this year.
Draup, an enterprise hiring analytics firm, builds its counts from public job listings and platforms such as LinkedIn.
why_it_matters_hint: Banks are hiring for people who can run teams of AI agents and keep them in check, but the headline percentage comes from a small starting number in one firm's count of job postings.
event_date: CNBC report published Friday 2 Oct 2026; data covers 2025 and 2026 so far
notes: Original outlet CNBC blocked (HTTP 403, edge error page); written from PYMNTS, which summarises the CNBC report and the Draup data. The CNBC article and the Draup data were not read directly.
